companion_benefits: Helps fruit trees, nightshades, brassicas, and carrots. Helped by carrots, tomatoes, marigolds, and mints. Strong scent confuses carrot and onion flies when inter-planted with carrots.
antagonist_reasons: Inhibits growth of beans and peas.

companion_benefits: Helps tomatoes and parsley. Helped by aster family flowers, dill, coriander, basil, comfrey, marigolds, and nasturtiums.
antagonist_reasons: Onion, garlic, and potatoes are incompatible with asparagus.

companion_benefits: Helps cucumber and strawberries. Helped by celery, strawberries, and grains. Fixes nitrogen in the soil.
antagonist_reasons: Lettuce, potato, tomato, other legumes, crucifers, and cucurbits increase sclerotinia in the soil and should be avoided before and after snap beans.

companion_benefits: Helps radishes and corn. The corn stalk provides a pole for beans to climb, and beans then give nitrogen back to the soil. Traditional Three Sisters planting with corn and squash.
antagonist_reasons: Stunts growth of brassicas and kohlrabi.

companion_benefits: Helps strawberries and celery. Fixes nitrogen in the soil.

Helps bush beans, cabbage, lettuce, kohlrabi, onions, brassicas, and passion fruit. Helped by bush beans, onions, kohlrabi, catnip, garlic, and mint. Leaves contain up to 25% magnesium — great for composting.
antagonist_reasons: Runner or pole beans and beets stunt each other's growth.

companion_benefits: Helped by a wide range of aromatic plants, alliums, and flowers. Thyme, nasturtiums, and onion showed good resistance to cabbage worm, weevil, and cabbage looper.
antagonist_reasons: Mustards, nightshades, pole beans, and strawberries are incompatible with brassicas.

companion_benefits: Helps lettuce. Helped by beets, dill, onions, tomato, turnip, and clover. Broccoli intercropped with lettuce was shown to be more profitable than either crop alone. Turnip acts as a trap crop.
Helped by sage, thyme, and clover.

Helps beans and celery. Helped by clover, calendula, chamomile, larkspur, nasturtiums, dill, onions, beets, mint, rosemary, sage, and thyme. Nasturtiums repel cabbage moths. If using clover, sow after cabbage transplant to avoid affecting yield.
antagonist_reasons: Grapes should be avoided near cabbage.

companion_benefits: Helps tomatoes, alliums, beans, leeks, lettuce, and onions. Helped by alliums, rosemary, wormwood, sage, beans, and flax. Tomatoes grow better with carrots nearby. Alliums inter-planted with carrots confuse onion and carrot flies. Aromatic companions repel carrot fly.
antagonist_reasons: Dill stunts carrot growth; parsnips compete and share diseases; radish competes for space.

companion_benefits: Helped by spinach, peas, marigolds, and sunflower. Helps beans, celery, spinach, and peas. Peas and spinach show mutualism with cauliflower.
Helps bush beans, brassicas, and cucumber. Helped by cosmos, daisies, snapdragons, leeks, tomatoes, cauliflower, and cabbage.
antagonist_reasons: Aster flowers can transmit the aster yellows disease to celery.

companion_benefits: Helps brassicas and passion fruit.

Helps beans, cucurbits, and soybeans. Helped by sunflowers, dill, legumes, peanuts, cucurbits, clover, and amaranth. Provides beans with a trellis. Protected from predators and dryness by cucurbits in the Three Sisters technique.
antagonist_reasons: Tomato and corn attract shared pests; celery competes for nutrients.

companion_benefits: Helped by nasturtiums, radishes, marigolds, sunflowers, peas, beans, chamomile, and dill. Sowing 2–3 radish seeds with cucumbers repels cucumber beetles. One study showed a 75% reduction in cucumber beetles with concurrent amaranth seeding.
antagonist_reasons: Potatoes compete and share diseases; aromatic herbs may inhibit cucumber growth.

companion_benefits: Helps and is helped by corn and grain sorghum. Large leaves shade soil and protect corn from predators and dryness in the Three Sisters technique.
Helps beans, peppers, tomatoes, and passion fruit. Helped by marigolds, catnip, tarragon, mints, and thyme. Marigolds deter nematodes.
Helps and is helped by onion, beets, aromatic plants, and cucumbers.
Helps carrots, celery, onions, tomato, and passion fruit. Helped by carrots and clover. Shares allium companion traits — deters carrot fly and other pests.
antagonist_reasons: Swiss chard is incompatible with leeks.

companion_benefits: Hosts nitrogen-fixing bacteria, fertilizing neighboring plants. Helps beets, lettuce, okra, potato, cabbage, carrots, tomatoes, brassicas, corn, and cucumbers. Rosemary and peppermint extracts are used in organic sprays for beans. Summer savory and potatoes repel bean beetles.
antagonist_reasons: Alliums inhibit legume growth; gladiolas are incompatible.

companion_benefits: Helps beets, beans, okra, onions, radish, broccoli, and carrots. Helped by radish, dill, kohlrabi, onions, beans, cucumbers, strawberries, thyme, nasturtiums, alyssum, and cilantro. Broccoli intercropped with lettuce was more profitable than either crop alone.
antagonist_reasons: Celery may inhibit lettuce growth; cabbage, cress, and parsley compete.

companion_benefits: Helps beans, cabbage, cauliflower, fruit trees, grapes, radish, Brussels sprouts, and turnips. Repels various pests.
Helped by carrots, alliums, and aromatic mints like basil and oregano.
antagonist_reasons: Black walnuts produce juglone, which is toxic to nightshades. Beans, corn, fennel, dill, and brassicas are also incompatible.

companion_benefits: Helps sweet potato, tomatoes, and peppers. Helped by beans, lettuce, squash, sweet potato, and peppers. Okra and sweet potato are mutually beneficial when planted simultaneously.
Helps beets, brassicas, carrots, lettuce, cucumbers, and strawberries. Helped by carrots, dill, summer savory, chamomile, and pansy. Strong scent deters many pests.
antagonist_reasons: Onions inhibit growth of lentils, peas, and beans.

companion_benefits: Helps fruit trees. When left to flower and seed, parsnip attracts a variety of predatory insects — particularly helpful under fruit trees against codling moth and light brown apple moth.

Helps and is helped by turnip, cauliflower, garlic, and mints. Intercropped with turnip, cauliflower, or garlic — mutual suppression of growth occurs but profit per land area used is increased. Reduces Colorado potato beetle density.

Helps okra. Helped by beans, tomatoes, okra, geraniums, petunias, sunflowers, onions, crimson clover, basil, and field mustard. Marjoram and basil ground cover raises humidity for peppers. Sunflowers shelter beneficial insects, lowering thrips populations.
antagonist_reasons: Kale, cabbage, Brussels sprouts, and other brassicas are incompatible with peppers.

companion_benefits: Helped by horseradish, beans, marigolds, peas, onion, garlic, thyme, and clover. Horseradish increases disease resistance and repels the potato bug. Garlic is more effective than fungicides on late potato blight. Peas reduce the density of Colorado potato beetles.
antagonist_reasons: Tomatoes and potatoes share blight disease. Cucumbers, squash, pumpkin, raspberries, and sunflowers compete or share diseases.

companion_benefits: Helps corn and beans as part of the traditional Three Sisters partnership. Helped by buckwheat, catnip, oregano, tansy, radishes, and nasturtiums. Radishes used as trap crop for flea beetles. Nasturtiums repel squash bugs.
antagonist_reasons: Potatoes compete with pumpkins and share diseases.

companion_benefits: Helps squash, eggplant, cucumber, lettuce, peas, and beans. Helped by chervil, lettuce, and nasturtiums. Acts as a trap crop against flea beetles. Radishes grown with lettuce taste better.
antagonist_reasons: Grapes should be avoided near radishes.

companion_benefits: Helps corn and sunflower. A mixture of corn, mungbean, and sunflower was found to rid soybeans of aphids. Fixes nitrogen in the soil.
Helps brassicas and passion fruit. Helped by strawberries, peas, and beans. The peas and beans provide natural shade for the spinach.

Helps corn, beans, and okra. Helped by beans, buckwheat, borage, catnip, tansy, radishes, marigolds, and nasturtiums. Marigolds and nasturtiums repel squash bugs. Marigolds repel cucumber beetles. Can be used in the Three Sisters technique.
Mutually beneficial with okra when planted simultaneously.

Helped by asparagus, basil, beans, bee balm, oregano, parsley, marigold, alliums, garlic, borage, chives, and many more. Growing ~10 inches from basil can increase tomato yield by about 20%. Marigolds deter nematodes and whiteflies.
antagonist_reasons: Black walnut produces juglone which is toxic to tomatoes. Fennel releases growth inhibitors. Corn and tomatoes share the corn earworm. Dill attracts tomato hornworm. Potatoes share blight disease. Brassicas compete for nutrients.

companion_benefits: Helps peas and broccoli. Helped by hairy vetch and peas. Turnips act as a trap crop for broccoli. Intercropped with peas, mutual growth suppression occurs but profit per land area is increased.
antagonist_reasons: Hedge mustard and knotweed are incompatible with turnips.

companion_benefits: Helped by clover, chives, garlic, leeks, nasturtium, southernwood, daffodils, and comfrey. Chives said to prevent apple scab after 3 years planted at the base of apple trees.
antagonist_reasons: Cedar causes apple-cedar rust. Walnut roots produce growth inhibitors that apple trees are sensitive to.

companion_benefits: Helped by peppers.
antagonist_reasons: A fungus that peppers are prone to can infect apricot trees causing significant harm — monitor closely if planting together.

companion_benefits: Helped by oak and pine trees (which create the acidic soil blueberries need), strawberries and dewberries (ground cover), clover (nitrogen), yarrow and bay laurel (repel insects).
antagonist_reasons: Tomatoes are incompatible with blueberries.

companion_benefits: Helped by alliums, tansy, nasturtiums, marigolds, marjoram, lemon balm, mustards, dandelions, and borage.
Helped by hyssop, basil, beans, chives, geraniums, mustards, oregano, clover, peas, and blackberries.
antagonist_reasons: Cabbage, garlic, and radishes are incompatible with grapes.

companion_benefits: Helped by chamomile, pigweed, summer savoury, and sow thistle.
Helps potatoes, beets, Swiss chard, carrots, spinach, strawberries, eggplants, onions, leeks, and lettuce.
antagonist_reasons: Cucurbits, maize, cowpea, sorghum, okra, and sweet potatoes are incompatible with passion fruit.

companion_benefits: Helped by aromatic plants.
Helped by caraway, bush beans, lupin, onions, sage, thyme, and borage. Thyme planted next to strawberries helps produce more fruit quickly. Borage deters pests and attracts pollinators.
antagonist_reasons: Brassicas inhibit strawberry growth. Verticillium-susceptible species (tomatoes, potatoes, eggplant, peppers, melons, okra, mint, roses) can spread Verticillium wilt to strawberries.

companion_benefits: Helps coriander. Not to be confused with star anise, which is an entirely different species.

Helps tomato, peppers, oregano, asparagus, petunias, and grapes. Helped by chamomile and anise. Said to make tomatoes taste better. Growing ~10 inches from tomatoes can increase yield by 20%. Chamomile and anise increase essential oils in basil.
antagonist_reasons: Common rue and thyme inhibit basil growth.

companion_benefits: Good companion for almost everything, especially beans, strawberry, cucurbits, fruit trees, tomatoes, and cabbage. Attracts predatory insects and honeybees. Predict a square metre for its adult size.
Helps strawberries. Attracts parasitic wasps and parasitic flies.
antagonist_reasons: Dill is incompatible with caraway.

companion_benefits: Helps eggplant. Repels flea beetles, ants, and aphids.
Helps most herbs, brassicas, cucumber, wheat, onion, and cabbage. Growing near herbs increases their oil production. Attracts hoverflies and wasps.
Helps radish, lettuce, and broccoli. Loves shade; grows well with shade-tolerant food plants. Makes radishes grown near it taste spicier.
antagonist_reasons: Attracts aphids which can affect radish — monitor when planting together.

companion_benefits: Helps apples, carrots, grapes, roses, tomatoes, and brassicas. Helped by carrots. Said to prevent apple scab after 3 years planting at base of apple trees. Shares companion traits with all alliums.
antagonist_reasons: Inhibits growth of beans and peas.

companion_benefits: Helps anise, cabbage, spinach, lettuce, and tomato. Helped by beans and peas. Attracts hoverflies which reduce pest populations in cabbages.

Helps brassicas, corn, fennel, lettuce, onions, and cucumbers. Helped by fennel. One of the few plants said to grow well with fennel. Attracts tiger swallowtail butterflies, hoverflies, wasps, ladybugs, and honeybees.
antagonist_reasons: Dill cross-pollinates with and stunts the growth of carrots.

companion_benefits: Helps and is helped by dill. Attracts ladybugs, syrphid fly, and tachinid fly which reduce aphids through predation. Dill has a stabilizing effect on fennel seed.
antagonist_reasons: Fennel is allelopathic to most garden plants — inhibiting growth, causing bolting, or killing many plants. Use with great caution.

companion_benefits: Helps carrots and potatoes. Contains tannin and linseed oils which repel the Colorado potato bug.

Helped by tarragon and peas. Helps vetch, brassicas, beets, roses, tomatoes, cucumbers, lettuce, celery, peas, and potatoes. Peas and garlic together suppress each other slightly but profit per area is higher. Tarragon makes garlic grow rapidly. More effective than fungicides on late potato blight.
antagonist_reasons: Grapes should be avoided near garlic.

companion_benefits: Helps brassicas, cabbage, and grapes. Attracts honeybees, butterflies, and bees. Stimulates growth of grapes.
antagonist_reasons: Hyssop inhibits radish growth.

companion_benefits: Helps chamomile, lettuce, brassicas, onions, tomatoes, oregano, thyme, marjoram, sage, rosemary, basil, lemon balm, and squash. Attracts butterflies, hummingbirds, and bees.
Helps eggplant. Reduces cutworms in eggplant in laboratory trials.
Helps beans. Thought to improve the health of almost all plants — considered a 'magic bullet' of companion planting, like borage and geraniums. Attracts ichneumonid wasps and ground beetles.
antagonist_reasons: Rhubarb is incompatible with lovage.

companion_benefits: Helped by basil. Helps grapes, tomatoes, peppers, pumpkin, and many other plants. Provides ground cover and humidity for peppers when spread among them. Attracts syrphidae, reducing aphids through predation.
Helps asparagus, corn, and tomatoes. Helped by apple and rose. Sacrificially attracts insects that feed on tomatoes.
antagonist_reasons: Alliums and lettuce are incompatible with parsley.

companion_benefits: Helps alliums, brassicas, cabbage, peas, and tomatoes. Repels cabbage flies. Has same general companion properties as other mints.
Helps cabbage, beans, brassicas, carrots, and thyme. Deters cabbage flies and repels many bean parasites.
Helps brassicas, rosemary, cabbage, beans, Brussels sprouts, carrots, strawberry, tomato, and marjoram. Attracts honeybees and cabbage butterflies.
antagonist_reasons: Avoid any member of the allium family and common rue near sage.

companion_benefits: Helps brassicas and fruit trees. Controls cabbage moths and malaria mosquitoes.
Helps alliums, brassicas, cabbage, peas, and tomatoes. Controls ants and aphids.
Helps chamomile, mint, broccoli, tomatoes, valerian, angelica, marjoram, sage, and peppermint.
Helps beans, melon, and onions. Also delays germination of certain foul herbs.
Helps most vegetables, especially eggplant. Its scent is disliked by most pests. Thought to have nurse plant properties that enhance the growth and flavor of crops grown with it.
Helps brassicas, cabbage, eggplant, potato, strawberry, tomato, and Brussels sprouts. Attracts Syrphidae, reducing aphids through predation.
Helps brassicas and carrots. Repels ants.
antagonist_reasons: Wormwood should be used with caution around most vegetables since it contains toxins.

companion_benefits: Helps many plants and most aromatic plants. May increase essential oil production in some herbs. Improves soil quality — use leaves to enrich compost or as mulch. Attracts syrphidae, reducing aphids through predation.
Helps lettuce. Attracts Syrphidae and most beneficial insects, helping reduce aphids through predation.
Attracts Syrphidae, helping reduce aphids through predation.
Helps tomato. Attracts bees.
Attracts Syrphidae, helping reduce aphids through predation.
Helps roses, lavender, echinacea, aster, and foxglove.
Helps roses, corn, peppers, and grapes. Acts as a trap crop, attracting pests away from roses and grapevines.
antagonist_reasons: Keep away from solanaceous plants like eggplant and tobacco. Distracts beet leafhoppers that carry the curly top virus.

companion_benefits: Helps beans and cabbage.

Helps cucurbits, brassica, lettuce, rosemary, dill, strawberry, and rose. Helped by summer savory and rose. This wildflower is a legume, hosting nitrogen-fixing bacteria. Planting near roses causes them to grow vigorously.
antagonist_reasons: Incompatible with tomatoes and other solanaceae.

id: Tagetes patula / T. erecta / T. minuta
companion_benefits: Helps most plants — especially tomatoes, peppers, cucurbits, potatoes, roses, alliums, and brassicas. Helped by rose. French marigolds (T. patula) produce a pesticidal chemical from roots lasting years after they are gone. Mexican marigolds (T. erecta) inhibit growth of tender herbs. Stinking Roger (T. minuta) is effective against perennial weeds.

Helped by predatory insects. Helps beans, squash, tomatoes, fruit trees, brassicas, radish, and cucumbers. Among the best at attracting predatory insects. Trap crop for aphids — deters many pests of cucurbits.
antagonist_reasons: Incompatible with cauliflower.

companion_benefits: Helps alliums, onions, and roses. Helped by roses. Helps alliums and onions which in turn repel the white butterfly.
Helps cucurbits (squash, pumpkins, cucumbers) and asparagus. Acts as a trap crop almost identical to geraniums in function.
Helps plants prone to aphids, especially lettuce, tomato, and rose. Attracts hoverflies that reduce aphid populations.
Helped by chives, garlic, and marigolds.

Helps peppers, corn, cucumber, soybeans, tomatoes, and swan plant. Helped by swan plant. Grown as a companion for corn before modern Europeans arrived in the Americas. Ants herd aphids onto sunflowers, keeping them off neighboring plants. Acts as a trap plant for thrips on bell peppers.
antagonist_reasons: Pole beans are incompatible with sunflowers.

antagonists: Plants that attract aphids and spider mites
companion_benefits: Helps sunflower. Helped by sunflower and basil. Attracts the monarch butterfly during spring and summer. Basil repels pests such as aphids that the swan plant attracts.
antagonist_reasons: Avoid placing near plants that already attract aphids and spider mites.

companion_benefits: Helped by sweet alyssum, lobelia, roses, lavender, and catmint. An annual climbing plant; makes a good decoration for garden or fence.
antagonist_reasons: Incompatible with brassica, spinach, silverbeet, and salads.

companion_benefits: Helps beans, cucurbits, raspberries and relatives, roses, corn, and fruit trees. Attracts ladybugs and honeybees. Reputed to repel herbivorous insects.
antagonist_reasons: Toxic to people and many animals — do not plant where livestock browse.

companion_benefits: Helps beans, tomatoes, and peppers. Attracts hummingbirds that eat whiteflies; also attracts pollinators.
Helps cotton by reducing pest populations. Attracts assassin bug, big-eyed bug, ladybug, and parasitic wasps. A good crop to improve soil; fixes nitrogen.
antagonist_reasons: Alfalfa has allelopathic effects on tomato seedlings. Incompatible with fava beans.

companion_benefits: Helps beans, corn, cucumber, eggplant, lettuce, marigold, melon, and sunflower. Encourages growth of corn and squash. Fixes nitrogen in the soil.
Helps many types of grass including Kentucky bluegrass. Helped by European alder (sacrifice plant), hairy vetch, crownvetch, and sericea lespedeza.
antagonist_reasons: Black walnut produces juglone, which is harmful to all nightshade plants including Datura, eggplant, mandrake, deadly nightshade, capsicum, potato, tomato, and petunia. Also incompatible with apple trees.
